question: In 1992, the Municipality of Tortora (Cosenza) issued an authorisation for the construction of a nonhazardous waste treatment plant on the Calabrian side of the Noce river in the district of San Sago. Operations at the plant, however, remain on hold because the authorisation has been suspended since 2013.

The plant is located fewer than 200 metres from the 'Valle del Noce' SCI/ZAC IT9210265 protected area and is also in the immediate vicinity of several sites forming part of the Natura 2000 network. On 23 April 2021, the Basilicata Region's Environment and Energy Department issued a favourable opinion to its assessment of the impact of the 'hazardous and non-hazardous waste disposal plant' proposed by Co.Gi.Fe.

Ambiente s.r.l. The department deemed it not necessary to conduct an impact assessment procedure for the plant and, therefore, did not conduct an in-depth evaluation of the categories of waste it was to treat.

By an act issued by Commissioner Paolo Cagnoli on 19 October 2023, the Ministry of the Environment gave comprehensive environmental authorisation for the San Sago special and nonspecial liquid waste disposal plant. Can the Commission say whether the Region of Basilicata is complying with Article 6 of Directive 92/43/EEC (Habitats Directive)?
answer: The Commission has no specific information about the project referred to by the Honourable Member, which would be located outside the Natura 2000 site IT9210265.

According to Article 6(3) of the Habitats Directive (1), any plan or project that is likely to have a significant impact on a Natura 2000 site, either individually or in combination with other plans or projects, must be subject to an assessment of its impacts in view of the site's conservation objectives.

In the light of the conclusions of the assessment of the implications for the site, the competent national authorities shall agree to the plan or project only after having ascertained that it will not adversely affect the integrity of the site concerned and, if appropriate, after having obtained the opinion of the general public.

The Commission published several guidance documents to help Member States’ authorities implement the above-mentioned provisions (2). Italy has transposed these provisions in its national legislation (3) and, in 2019, adopted tailored national guidelines to facilitate and ensure their consistent implementation across its regions (4).

The Region of Basilicata has also adopted relevant and up-todate rules transposing the above provisions and guidelines (5). Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, Member States’ authorities are primarily responsible to ensure compliance with EU law, including in relation to applying the above-mentioned provisions to the project in question.
